findings.observed: banner-en.png (shows "Financing that fits your plans / Competitive rates. Clear terms. No surprises.")
findings.expected: Serve a French banner (banner-fr.png) with « Un financement adapté à vos projets — Taux concurrentiels. Modalités claires. Aucune surprise. »
findings.description: The French landing page uses the English banner image whose embedded text is in English.
Subtitle uses informal "tu" while the title and rest of the site use "vous".
"Appliquer pour" is a well-known anglicism (calque of "apply for") flagged by the OQLF.
Footer copyright notice is left in English on French pages.
The required-field error for "Nom complet" is shown in English on the French form, while the other fields' errors are translated.

findings.expected: Let the button grow with its content (remove fixed width / overflow hidden), or shorten to « Soumettre la demande ».
findings.description: The French submit button label is clipped to "Soumettre ma demande" (scrollWidth 290 > clientWidth 210, overflow hidden, nowrap).
"E-mail" is a France-French usage; Canadian French uses "courriel" (OQLF recommendation).

findings.observed: Merci. Votre demande pour {montant} a été reçue.
findings.expected: Merci. Votre demande de 15 000,00 $ a été reçue.
findings.description: The French confirmation shows the raw template variable {montant} instead of the amount; the placeholder name was translated so it is not substituted.
The transactions section heading is left in English on the French dashboard.
Transaction dates on the French dashboard use the US MM/DD/YYYY order, which is ambiguous and wrong for fr-CA (English uses ISO 2026-09-15). Affects all rows.
In French, zero takes the singular; the English plural rule was applied to the French count.
"Balance" for an account balance is an anglicism; the correct banking term in Canadian French is "solde".
A bank "statement" is a "relevé"; "déclaration" means a declaration (e.g., tax return), which changes the meaning.
The "Estimer un nouveau prêt" link on the French dashboard points to the English calculator, switching the user to English.

findings.expected: Use the French counterpart of promo-a.png showing « Taux variable : 5,2 % ».
findings.description: The French page shows a different promo image advertising a fixed rate of 4.9%, contradicting its own alt text and the English page's variable 5.2% rate.
The estimated monthly payment on the French calculator uses English currency formatting (leading $, decimal point).
The checkbox label says "Pay now" in French, the opposite of "Pay later", and contradicts its help text about deferring the first payment.

findings.observed: Aucune accusation pour un remboursement anticipé.
findings.expected: Aucuns frais ne s'appliquent en cas de remboursement anticipé.
findings.description: "Charges" (fees) was translated as "accusation" (criminal charge/accusation), which is wrong in a banking context.

findings.expected: Taux variable de 5,2 %, sous réserve de l'approbation du crédit.
findings.description: The French rate note drops the "subject to credit approval" condition.
The modal's "Close" action was translated as the adjective "proche" (near) instead of the verb "fermer".
The French application confirmation page declares its document language as English, unlike the other French pages (fr-CA).

findings.expected: Parse amounts using fr-CA conventions (space thousands separator, comma decimal) on the French form.
findings.description: An in-range amount typed in Canadian French format (15 000,50) is rejected as out of range on the French form, even though the error message itself uses that format.
